newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share index closed lower on Tuesday as short-term profit-taking set in after Monday's sharp gains, brokers said.
The B index shaved off 0.92 points or 0.57 percent to finish at 159.34 on turnover of HK$91.4 million against HK$93.2 million on Monday.
The A share market recouped early losses to end higher, helped by strong speculative buying demand for Shenzhen-based real estate issues, brokers said.
The domestic currency A share index rose 3.38 points or 0.72 percent to 469.90, with turnover expanding to 9.7 billion yuan from Monday's 8.2 billion yuan.
Both indices gained more than four percent on Monday on an extended rebound after recent government anti-speculation measures caused sharp losses, brokers said.
"Some impatient investors cashed in on yesterday's steep rise, fearing a repeat of recent market falls triggered by Beijing's crackdown," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Beijing last month announced a series of measures designed to eliminate excessive speculation, including banning state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading.
The B share market was also dampened by a Hong Kong newspaper report which said China's central government has further plans to depress share prices, brokers said.

Hong Kong's South China Morning Post reported on Tuesday that China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong has vowed to take further action to stop speculation and punish officials guilty of improper conduct.
"Beijing may punish some institutions to issue a warning this time, but it will be good for the markets in the long run," an analyst at a foreign investment bank in Shenzhen said.
Brokers said the B index will likely edge higher in coming sessions, barring any major negative news.
On the B share market, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd was the most actively traded stock on volume of 2.6 million shares.
The share lost HK$0.03 to close at HK$6.92 on profit-taking, brokers said.
On the A share market, Shenzhen Nanyou Property was the best performer, reaching its 10 percent limit-up to close at 15.90 yuan on volume of 29 million shares.
The stock was also the most actively traded A share.
